absent: Locking and concurrency rules for nested control-area access, MSR list handling and TLB requests.
Full layouts of the nested control area, virtual-CPU structures, segment descriptors and MSR entries.
Entry-failure and abort-code definitions beyond the default, directory-pointer and host-load cases.
Behavior of unrouted helpers for control-register writes, descriptor programming, MMU setup, guest memory access and performance monitoring.
Exact maximum MSR list size and secondary execution control bit assignments.

findings.text: Globally visible helper adjusts the virtual CPU interrupt shadow state for STI and move-SS blocking.
Globally visible helper records a new EFER value for the virtual CPU and refreshes related entry controls and user-return MSR selection.
Globally visible lookup maps an MSR number to its per-VMX user-return slot when present, otherwise reports absence.

Pending-event saving into the nested control area clears vectoring for triple-fault exits and for double-fault exits. Otherwise an injected exception has priority, then an injected NMI, then an injected interrupt, else vectoring is cleared. Soft exceptions record an exit instruction length and soft type, hard exceptions use hard type, error codes propagate with a delivery marker, NMIs use NMI type with validity, soft interrupts use soft type with entry length while external interrupts use external type.

Interrupt classification masks validity, type and vector before comparing against an expected valid typed vector, with wrappers specializing the check to hard exceptions and to the double-fault vector.
The exit-reason accessor derives the VT extension area from the generic virtual CPU object and returns its stored exit reason.

Nested-exit host loading proceeds in order: EFER selection and application, stack and instruction pointers with fixed flags and cleared shadow, control-register ownership refresh and host control-register load, MMU reset with host page-table base load and transition TLB handling, system-enter and descriptor-table reload with bound and CET and PAT and performance handling, segment reconstruction, then debug reset with host MSR load and emulation-needed recomputation.

Host EFER honors a load-EFER exit control when set, otherwise derives long-mode bits from an address-size control, then applies the result through the EFER setter. Owned control-register bits are refreshed before loading host values.

Host reload establishes stack pointer, instruction pointer, fixed flags and cleared shadow, releases nested extended-paging MMU context, loads host page-table base with directory-pointer handling, performs transition TLB handling, programs system-enter state and descriptor-table bases with full limits, optionally clears bound configuration, selects CET state from host or guest copies per control, and conditionally restores PAT and performance global control.

Host segments are rebuilt flat with full limits for code and data. Code is executable readable present with long or default-big mode from address size, data is writable present with default-big and granularity bits, filesystem and kernel GS segments additionally carry host bases, the task register carries host base with a small limit, and the descriptor-table register is zeroed and marked unusable.
Host finalization resets the debug control register and guest debug control, attempts loading host MSRs from the exit list, and recomputes whether emulation is required.
Exiting nested execution returns the active memory-management context to the root context.

MSR list loading walks a guest-physical entry array bounded by a maximum atomic-switch count, failing when the bound is reached, when a guest read fails, when per-entry validation fails, or when the emulated write fails, returning success or one past the failing index.
Load-time MSR validation rejects filesystem base, kernel GS base and SMM monitor control entries as unsupported, plus any entry rejected by common checks.

Page-table-base loading validates legality with a default entry-failure code on rejection, reloads directory pointers only for PAE paging without nested extended paging with a distinct directory-pointer failure code, then records the base, marks it dirty, reinitializes the memory manager and, without nested paging, notifies of the new directory.

Nested transition TLB handling services Hyper-V requests first, then when virtual-processor identifiers are not exposed requests a guest flush, otherwise on entry with a changed identifier records it and requests a guest flush, otherwise when no separate guest tag exists requests a current-context flush.

A separate guest TLB tag is present when extended paging is enabled or when virtual-processor identifiers are exposed and a second-level identifier has been allocated. Exposure is determined by the secondary execution control for identifiers.
CET state writes only touch branch-tracking state when that feature is exposed to the guest and only touch shadow-stack pointers when shadow stacks are exposed.

Interrupt-shadow updates preserve unrelated interruptibility bits, clear both STI and move-SS blocking, set at most one of them per requested mask with move-SS preferred, and skip the control-structure write when unchanged.

Control-structure writes validate the field encoding then divert to enlightened handling when enlightenments are active, otherwise perform the native write, with wide writes on narrow hosts split across two halves. One enlightened variant stores into the shared page and clears the matching clean marker, while the fallback variant discards the write.

EFER setting is a no-op without hardware EFER support, otherwise records the value, synchronizes the sixty-four-bit entry-mode bit with long-mode-active status, and refreshes user-return selection. That selection enables system-call MSRs only in long mode with system-call extensions, refreshes EFER per transition logic, enables timestamp auxiliary on relevant features, conditions transaction-control handling on host capability, and marks user-return state not loaded.

Transition EFER logic forces non-executable without extended paging, ignores system-call and long-mode bits outside long mode while honoring system-call extensions in long mode, uses atomic switching when the CPU supports EFER loading or when extended-paging non-executable differs from host, clearing long-mode-enable when inactive and adding or removing the atomic entry on equality with host, otherwise falls back to a masked user-return entry combining guest and host bits.

Atomic MSR switching prefers dedicated entry and exit controls for EFER and performance global control when supported, otherwise maintains guest and host autoload lists with count fields kept in sync, appending new slots up to a maximum and compacting on removal by moving the last entry, and explicitly disables event sampling before arranging its switch.
User-return MSR configuration looks up the slot and, when found, records whether the MSR should be loaded into hardware.
Host state loading aborts the virtual CPU when host directory-pointer loading fails and when host MSR list loading reports failure, using a distinct abort reason for each case.

Host reload uses fixed architectural facts: flags set to the fixed pattern, shadow cleared, descriptor-table limits full range, task-register limit small, debug register seven set to its default masked value with debug control cleared, and bound configuration cleared to zero when its control is set.
Interrupt-shadow state distinguishes STI blocking from move-SS blocking, and event vectoring distinguishes validity, hard versus soft exception and interrupt types, and error-code delivery.
